# Password Generator 1.6.0

Password Generator 1.6.0 is the first unified native release for Android, Windows, and macOS.

## New platforms

- Added a native Windows application built with C++20 and Win32/Common Controls.
- Added a native macOS application built with Swift and AppKit.
- Both desktop applications intentionally avoid third-party runtime libraries and cross-platform UI frameworks.

## Feature parity

Windows and macOS now provide the same core generator behavior as Android:

- password length from 4 to 64 characters;
- lowercase, uppercase, digits, and symbols;
- at least one character from every enabled group;
- optional exclusion of visually similar characters;
- optional exclusion of duplicate characters;
- 16, 24, and 32 character presets;
- password-strength scoring;
- hidden password by default with explicit reveal;
- copy to the native clipboard;
- saved non-secret generator preferences;
- English and Russian UI.

## Privacy and security

- Passwords are generated locally with the operating system cryptographic RNG: SecureRandom on Android, BCryptGenRandom on Windows, and SecRandomCopyBytes on macOS.
- Generated passwords are never persisted.
- Desktop bounded random selection uses rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias.
- Clipboard cleanup waits 60 seconds and clears only Password Generator's own still-current copied value.
- Revealed passwords enable the strongest practical native capture-exclusion mechanism available on each platform.
- The product remains offline, without analytics, advertising, tracking, accounts, telemetry, or cloud synchronization.

## Desktop signing status

- The Windows executable is published without Authenticode publisher signing in this release.
- The macOS application is ad-hoc signed for bundle integrity and sandbox entitlements, but it is not Developer ID signed or Apple-notarized.
- GitHub release checksums and artifact attestations are published for the desktop artifacts.
- Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper may therefore show an unknown/unidentified publisher warning on first launch.

## Unified product

Android, Windows, and macOS now share one public product version and common generator, privacy, and UX contracts while retaining fully native platform implementations.
